analysis.title: [GS] Midterm Elections (preview + 3 calls), Asia Conviction list changes, China Banks
key_insights: Midterm elections are on Tuesday. Polling shows national sentiment has swung by around 10-11pp toward Democrats, and prediction markets imply high odds Democrats win the House with a margin of around 236 seats, wider than either party has had in several years.

GS expects the data center theme in some campaigns to fade after the election because it ranks low among voter priorities. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, but a national moratorium looks unlikely under any outcome.
GS expects congressional focus to shift to AI regulation. A compromise codifying basic federal oversight and self-testing is possible, but restrictive regulation looks unlikely.
GS is hosting three Midterms calls on Nov 4: 8am ET first take, 10:15am ET views from DC and the trading floor, 11:30am ET election post mortem.

GS raised its crude forecasts. Dec26 Brent goes to $105/bbl from $90 and WTI to $94. 2027 average Brent goes to $88 from $80 and WTI to $78 from $73. The reasons are a large near-term risk premium from downside supply risks and a new global supply disruption allowance for the medium term, even though Mideast output continues to recover as expected.

US 3Q26 midseason earnings (Ben Snider): earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating. GS reads Q3 as showing AI investment spending still growing while the growth rate of AI capex is peaking.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue is still accelerating. Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT was 54% year/year in Q3, which GS reads as increasing signs of return on AI investments.
Elevated expectations and crowded positioning going into the quarter set a high bar for share prices. Q3 results also raised investor focus on AI disruption risk, particularly among TMT stocks.
Analysts continued to lift forward earnings estimates this season, but the rate of upward revisions has slowed.

China macro survey: more than half of respondents expect growth momentum to hold steady and one-third expect a slowdown. More than half expect similar consumption growth and one-third expect a further slowdown.

China survey: offshore investors lean toward property-price stability while onshore investors are more cautious. Most see a conventional PBOC policy rate cut over the next six months as a close call. Modest CNY gains are the consensus, with offshore investors more optimistic.
China survey: investors are broadly optimistic about AI's contribution to growth, but enthusiasm remains measured.

China banks 3Q26 first take: the five large banks beat expectations, with average PPOP growth of 16% and net profit growth of 7% year-over-year. Stabilizing net interest margins and solid bond investment gains gave capacity for accelerated risk disposal and a 47% average year-over-year rise in provision charges.

GS maintains Buy on CCB and BOC. It says CCB delivered a clean beat with robust earnings quality, and that reasonable earnings growth with contained balance-sheet risk should support sector valuations.
APAC Conviction List November update: adding Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel, removing NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and HK Exchanges.

Rating changes: Kia downgraded to Neutral after a 3Q26 operating profit miss on cost pressures likely to persist. China Jewelry: CTF upgraded to Buy and LF downgraded to Sell. Bicara Therapeutics (BCAX) downgraded to Sell with an $8 price target on competitive pressure in HNSCC.

A large batch of Asia tech and industrial results was flagged, including Murata, Kioxia, Mediatek, Innolight, CXMT, Panasonic, Lasertec, Yageo, Sumitomo Electric, Mitsubishi Electric, HOYA, Montage, Luxshare, Eoptolink, TDK, Tokyo Electron, Ibiden and Toto.

Most-read research includes a Kioxia read-across with the mid- to long-term NAND outlook intact and a Buy on SEC/Hynix, and a Korea memory pricing tracker with the 4Q26 DRAM ASP forecast for PC higher, server/mobile in line and NAND lower than GSe.
